key_insight: PAL converts lecture videos into interactive, context-aware learning sessions that adapt in real time to a learner’s evolving understanding, moving beyond static personalization to continuous, on-the-fly adaptation.
problem_solved: Addresses the limits of static adaptation in AI-driven education (predefined quizzes, fixed pacing, generic feedback) by enabling real-time, context-aware adjustments that respond to learners’ changing knowledge and engagement.
method: Multimodal ingestion of lecture videos (audio, transcript, slides) to extract concepts, timestamps, and question opportunities.
Learner modeling + real-time feedback loop: track performance and engagement metrics to select or generate microactivities, hints, and pacing adjustments on the fly.
Adaptive UI/runtime orchestration to deliver interactive elements (inline quizzes, summaries, targeted hints) and update content sequencing based on inferred learner state.
impact: PAL demonstrates a practical path for deploying real-time personalization in educational systems, offering ML practitioners a template for combining multimodal understanding, online learner models, and adaptive UX to boost engagement and learning outcomes.
visual_elements: System pipeline diagram: video -> multimodal extractor -> learner model -> adaptive content generator -> interactive player
Feedback loop infographic showing continuous assessment (quiz/response) updating the learner state and driving next content selection
Side-by-side UI mockup: original lecture video vs. PAL-enhanced interactive player with inline questions and hints
Bar/line chart illustrating expected gains (engagement, retention) or latency vs. personalization trade-offs
paper_authors: Megha Chakraborty, Darssan L. Eswaramoorthi, Madhur Thareja, Het Riteshkumar Shah, Finlay Palmer
